agents.summary: Query transformation is the art of turning a raw user query into one or more optimized search queries BEFORE hitting the vector DB. > Users write queries the way they think. Vector DBs need queries that match how documents are written.

agents.title: 08. Multi-Agent & Patterns: CHUNKING STRATEGIES (Part 1 of 3)

agents.title: 08. Multi-Agent & Patterns: Reranking
agents.summary: Reranking is a second-pass scoring step that takes an initial set of retrieved documents and re-orders them by TRUE relevance to the query — going far beyond simple vector similarity. > It is the single highest-impact improvement you can…

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Observability & Tracing
agents.summary: Observability = the ability to understand what your agent is doing at every step. Without it, debugging a production failure is like finding a needle in a haystack — blindfolded.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Cost Tracking & Budget Control
agents.summary: Every LLM call costs money. Without tracking, costs spiral out of control.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Semantic Cache
agents.summary: Cache LLM responses so that similar questions get the cached answer instead of calling the LLM again. Not just exact matches — semantically similar queries hit the cache too.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Rate Limiting & Throttling
agents.summary: Rate limiting controls how many requests a user/service can make in a time window. Without it, one misbehaving client can exhaust your API quota, causing everyone to experience failures.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Retry Logic & Exponential Backoff
agents.summary: APIs fail transiently — network hiccup, rate limit hit, server overload. Retry logic automatically retries failed calls with exponential backoff (increasing wait times) so temporary issues don't cause permanent failures.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Circuit Breaker
agents.summary: When a downstream service is failing repeatedly, a circuit breaker opens (stops sending requests) to prevent cascade failures. After a timeout it half-opens (tests one request) and if successful, closes (resumes normal traffic).

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Prompt Injection Guard
agents.summary: Prompt injection = an attacker embeds malicious instructions inside content your agent processes (documents, web pages, user inputs). The LLM "reads" the hidden instructions and executes them.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Input Validation
agents.summary: Every user input must be validated before it reaches the LLM or any tool. Validation checks: length, content type, allowed characters, banned topics, and structural integrity.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Output Guardrails
agents.summary: Even after validation, LLMs can generate harmful, biased, inaccurate, or off-brand content. Output guardrails check the LLM's response before sending it to the user.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: PII Detection & Masking
agents.summary: PII (Personally Identifiable Information) must never be stored in LLM context, logged, or returned to unauthorized users. PII detection finds it and masking anonymizes it.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Tool Safety Controls
agents.summary: Tools give agents real power — reading files, executing code, calling APIs, deleting records. This power must be constrained.

agents.title: 09. Production & Safety: Jailbreak Detection (Part 1 of 3)
agents.summary: Jailbreaks are attempts to bypass safety restrictions through creative prompting — roleplay scenarios, fictional framing, hypothetical questions, or social engineering. Detection identifies these patterns and refuses them.

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Document Versioning and Incremental Updates

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Fixed-Size Chunking (Character and Token-Based)
veerarag.summary: Fixed-size chunking splits documents into segments of a predetermined size — either by character count or token count — with an optional overlap between consecutive chunks.

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Recursive Character Text Splitting
veerarag.summary: Recursive Character Text Splitting is LangChain's most versatile and production-recommended chunking strategy.

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Sentence-Level Chunking
veerarag.summary: Sentence-level chunking uses NLP sentence boundary detection to split documents exactly at sentence boundaries, then groups sentences into chunks that fit within a size limit.

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Semantic Chunking (Embedding-Based Boundary Detection)

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Hierarchical Chunking (Parent-Child Chunks)
veerarag.summary: Hierarchical chunking creates a two-level chunk structure: large parent chunks (1024-4096 tokens) that preserve broad context, and small child chunks (128-512 tokens) derived from the parents.

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Sliding Window Chunking
veerarag.summary: Sliding window chunking creates chunks with significant overlap by sliding a fixed-size window across the document at a configurable step size.

veerarag.title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Chunk Size Selection — Tradeoffs
veerarag.summary: Chunk size is the single most impactful hyperparameter in RAG systems — more impactful than the choice of vector database or even the embedding model.

veerarag.title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: What Are Embeddings — Vector Representation of Text
veerarag.summary: Embeddings are dense, fixed-dimensional numerical vectors that represent the semantic meaning of text in a continuous geometric space.

veerarag.title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: Embedding Model Selection
veerarag.summary: Selecting the right embedding model is a critical architectural decision that affects retrieval quality, cost, latency, and maintenance burden.

veerarag.title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: Dense vs Sparse Embeddings
veerarag.summary: Dense embeddings (BERT-style, neural) represent text as a continuous vector where every dimension contributes to meaning — high-dimensional but compact, capturing semantic similarity even without lexical overlap.

veerarag.title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder
veerarag.summary: Bi-encoders encode query and document independently, producing separate vectors that are compared via dot product or cosine similarity.

veerarag.title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: Domain-Specific Embedding Fine-Tuning
veerarag.summary: General embedding models are trained on internet text and perform well on general queries but struggle with specialized domains: medical terminology (ICD codes, drug names), legal jargon (Latin terms, specific statute references),…

veerarag.summary: Embedding models evolve — OpenAI releases text-embedding-3 to replace text-embedding-ada-002, BGE releases new versions, sentence-transformers updates model weights.

veerarag.title: 03. Embeddings & Vector DBs: Vector DB Fundamentals — Collections, Namespaces, Distance Metrics
veerarag.summary: A vector database is a specialized storage engine designed to store, index, and query dense numerical vectors at scale with sub-millisecond latency.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: What Is Information Retrieval (IR)
veerarag.summary: Information Retrieval (IR) is the science of finding material — typically documents — that satisfies an information need from within large collections.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Boolean Retrieval Model
veerarag.summary: The Boolean retrieval model matches documents against Boolean expressions of query terms using AND, OR, NOT operators. A document is either relevant (1) or not (0) — no ranking.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Vector Space Model — TF-IDF & Cosine Similarity
veerarag.summary: The Vector Space Model (VSM) represents documents and queries as vectors in a high-dimensional term space (one dimension per unique vocabulary term). Each dimension's value is the TF-IDF weight of the corresponding term.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Probabilistic Retrieval Model
veerarag.summary: The probabilistic retrieval model formalises relevance as a probability. Given query Q, the goal is to estimate P(R=1 | D, Q) — the probability that document D is relevant to query Q.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Language Model for IR — Query Likelihood
veerarag.summary: The Language Model (LM) approach to IR treats each document as a probability distribution over words — a language model θ_D.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Bag-of-Words Assumption
veerarag.summary: The bag-of-words (BoW) assumption treats a document as an unordered multiset of terms — word order and grammatical structure are discarded.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: IR Evaluation Framework
veerarag.summary: IR evaluation requires a test collection: a document corpus, a set of queries (topics), and relevance judgements (qrels) — human-annotated labels indicating which documents are relevant to each query.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: TF-IDF — Deep Dive
veerarag.summary: Term Frequency (TF) measures how often a query term appears in a document. The intuition: a document that mentions "machine learning" 10 times is more likely about machine learning than one that mentions it once.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: BM25 — Mathematical Foundations
veerarag.summary: BM25 (Best Match 25) is the dominant classical retrieval function, derived from the Probabilistic Relevance Framework. Given a query Q = {q₁, q₂, ..., qₙ} and a document D, BM25 sums per-term scores.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: BM25 Variants and Extensions
veerarag.summary: BM25F (BM25 with Field weights) extends BM25 to multi-field documents (e.g., title, body, anchor text, URL).

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Inverted Index
veerarag.summary: An inverted index is the core data structure of every text search system. It maps terms (vocabulary entries) to the list of documents where they appear, optionally with frequency and position information.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Tokenisation and Text Preprocessing
veerarag.summary: Tokenisation converts raw text into a sequence of discrete tokens that the inverted index can index and BM25 can score.

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: BM25 Implementations
veerarag.summary: rank-bm25 is the most widely used pure-Python BM25 library. It provides three variants: BM25Okapi (standard BM25 with Robertson IDF), BM25Plus (BM25+ with δ lower bound on TF weight), and BM25L (normalised TF variant).

veerarag.title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Sparse Vector Representations
veerarag.summary: Text retrieval requires representing documents and queries as comparable vectors. Sparse vectors have dimensionality equal to the vocabulary size (|V| ~ 100K–1M+) but only a small fraction of dimensions are non-zero.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: What is JSON-RPC and Why MCP Uses It
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we learned that MCP is a standard "language" for AI agents and tools. Today we learn the exact grammar of that language — how messages are structured and sent.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: MCP Transport Layers (How Messages Travel)
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we learned the exact shape of JSON-RPC messages. Today we learn how those messages actually travel between the client and the server.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: MCP Primitives: Tools (The Most Important One)
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we learned how messages travel. Today we learn the most important thing you will build: Tools — the functions your AI agent can call.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: MCP Primitives: Resources (Data the Agent Can Read)
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we built Tools — things the agent can do. Today we learn about Resources — things the agent can read.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: MCP Primitives: Prompts (Reusable Prompt Templates)
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we learned about Resources. Today we cover the third and final primitive — Prompts — reusable fill-in-the-blank templates.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Building Your First MCP Server (Raw Python SDK)
veerarag.summary: In previous lessons we learned about Tools, Resources, and Prompts using FastMCP. Today we use the raw MCP Python SDK — the lower-level approach — so you understand exactly what happens under the hood.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Building MCP Servers with FastMCP (The Easy Way)
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we built a calculator with the raw SDK — lots of code, but very clear. Today we rebuild it with FastMCP in a fraction of the lines.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Building an MCP Client (Connecting to a Server)
veerarag.summary: In the last two lessons we built servers. Today we flip sides and learn how to write Python code that connects to and talks to an MCP server.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Connecting MCP to LangChain
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we built an MCP client from scratch. Today we let LangChain do the client work for us — and use our MCP tools inside a real AI agent.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Connecting MCP to LangGraph
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we connected MCP to LangChain agents. Today we go deeper with LangGraph — for building agents with persistent state, complex flows, and multi-step reasoning.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Connecting MCP to Google ADK
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we used LangGraph. Today we connect our MCP server to Google ADK — Google's own agent framework.

veerarag.title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Connecting MCP to OpenAI Agents SDK
veerarag.summary: In the last lesson we connected to Google ADK. Today we connect to the OpenAI Agents SDK — OpenAI's own agent framework.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph RAG Foundations
veerarag.summary: Graph RAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation) augments LLM generation by retrieving context from a structured knowledge graph rather than (or in addition to) a flat vector index.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Knowledge Graph Construction
veerarag.summary: Entity extraction is the process of identifying and classifying named entities (people, organisations, locations, products, concepts) in unstructured text — the first step in building a knowledge graph.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Data Structures for RAG
veerarag.summary: The property graph model is the dominant data structure for Graph RAG systems.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Databases for Graph RAG
veerarag.summary: Graph databases store, query, and traverse graph-structured data natively — unlike relational databases that require expensive JOIN operations for relationship traversal.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Community Detection Algorithms
veerarag.summary: Community detection partitions a graph into clusters (communities) of nodes that are more densely connected internally than externally.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Traversal & Retrieval
veerarag.summary: Graph traversal is the mechanism by which Graph RAG retrieves relevant context from a knowledge graph given a query.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval
veerarag.summary: Hybrid Graph-Vector Retrieval fuses two complementary retrieval signals: vector similarity (semantic closeness in embedding space) and graph traversal (structural relatedness via typed relationships).

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Entity Linking & Disambiguation
veerarag.summary: Entity Linking (EL) — also called Named Entity Disambiguation (NED) — is the process of mapping entity mentions in text to specific entries in a knowledge base.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Query Languages
veerarag.summary: Graph databases use specialised query languages designed for traversing relationships efficiently. Cypher (Neo4j) uses a declarative, ASCII-art pattern syntax ((n)-[:REL]->(m)) that is highly readable and optimised for property graphs.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: Microsoft GraphRAG Deep Dive
veerarag.summary: Microsoft GraphRAG (released 2024) is an end-to-end framework that constructs a hierarchical community graph from source documents, then uses that graph for both local (entity-centric) and global (theme-level) question answering.

veerarag.title: 08. GraphRAG: LightRAG
veerarag.summary: LightRAG (University of Hong Kong, 2024) is a Graph RAG framework designed for efficiency and simplicity while supporting both entity-level and relationship-level retrieval.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Evaluation & Metrics
veerarag.summary: RAGAS (Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment) is the industry-standard framework for evaluating RAG systems. It provides reference-free metrics (no human labels required) by using an LLM as a judge.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Evaluation, tracing & monitoring — learning path
veerarag.summary: Audience: You already know LLMs, RAG, agents, agentic AI basics.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: LLM Evaluation: Metrics, Methods, and LLM-as-a-Judge
veerarag.summary: Prereq: You understand LLM basics (tokenization, prompting, fine-tuning at a conceptual level).

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: RAG Evaluation: Retrieval, Generation, and End-to-End Metrics
veerarag.summary: A RAG pipeline is two systems chained together: a retriever that fetches context and a generator (LLM) that produces an answer from it.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Advanced RAG: Graph RAG, Agentic RAG, Self-RAG & Corrective RAG Evaluation
veerarag.summary: Prerequisite: You've read 02-rag-evaluation.md — faithfulness, context precision/recall, RAGAS, basic retrieval metrics.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: AI Agent Evaluation: Tasks, Tools, and Trajectories
veerarag.summary: Prerequisite: File 01 (LLM eval). You know BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity, and LLM-as-judge for single input/output pairs. > > Scope: Single autonomous agents.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Multi-Agent System Evaluation: Coordination, Communication, and Emergent Behavior
veerarag.summary: A single agent is one LLM making one decision per step. A multi-agent system (MAS) is N agents, each making decisions, plus a coordination layer that decides who speaks next, who sees what, and when to stop.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Agentic AI Evaluation: Autonomy, Safety, and Long-Horizon Tasks
veerarag.summary: Prerequisite: Files 04 (single-agent eval) and 05 (multi-agent eval).

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Golden Datasets: The Foundation of Trustworthy AI Evaluation
veerarag.summary: Prerequisite: Files 01–09. You understand how to score LLM, RAG, agent, and tool-calling outputs; you understand tracing and monitoring.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Evaluation Metrics · BM25 & Sparse Retrieval
veerarag.summary: IR evaluation requires both a set of retrieved documents and relevance judgements (qrels). Precision@K measures what fraction of the top-K retrieved documents are relevant: the higher, the fewer irrelevant results the user sees.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Graph RAG Evaluation
veerarag.summary: Evaluating Graph RAG systems requires metrics that go beyond standard RAG evaluation because the retrieval mechanism is graph-structured — meaning we must assess not just whether the answer is correct, but whether the right entities,…

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Evaluation & Benchmarking
veerarag.summary: Covers Complete Evaluation Framework, VISUAL 13: Evaluation Metrics Dashboard.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Retriever Evaluation
veerarag.summary: The Retriever is responsible for fetching relevant documents from a knowledge base. We evaluate HOW WELL it retrieves the RIGHT documents.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: Generation Evaluation
veerarag.summary: After retrieval, the LLM generates an answer from the retrieved context. We evaluate HOW GOOD that generated answer is.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: END-TO-END EVALUATION (Part 1 of 2)
veerarag.summary: Context Precision measures: _"Among the retrieved context chunks, how many were actually NEEDED to answer the question?"_ It evaluates context quality from the perspective of relevance to the ground truth answer.

veerarag.title: 09. Evaluation: END-TO-END EVALUATION (Part 2 of 2)
veerarag.summary: LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (like GPT-4) to evaluate the quality of generated answers. It acts as an automated human evaluator.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: RAG Failure Modes & Debugging
veerarag.summary: RAG failures fall into five distinct categories, each with different root causes and fixes. Understanding the failure taxonomy is essential for systematic debugging — without a framework, engineers waste hours tuning the wrong component.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Security & Governance
veerarag.summary: Multi-tenant RAG systems (SaaS products, enterprise portals) must ensure that Tenant A cannot retrieve Tenant B's documents.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: LangChain RAG Patterns — RetrievalQA vs LCEL
veerarag.summary: LangChain has two generations of RAG abstractions. RetrievalQA (legacy): a high-level chain that wraps retriever + LLM + prompt into a single object — easy to use but hard to customize, instrument, or extend.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Complete Production RAG Reference Architecture
veerarag.summary: Covers ① Full System Design, ④ Complete Architecture Visual.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Performance & Scalability
veerarag.summary: Production RAG systems must meet strict latency SLAs — typically P95 < 2 seconds.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Performance and Scalability
veerarag.summary: BM25 query latency depends on corpus size, posting list lengths, and early termination. For a corpus of N documents with vocabulary V, the worst-case cost is O(Σ df(q_i)) per query — summing posting list lengths over all query terms.

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Failure Modes & Debugging
veerarag.summary: Graph RAG systems have failure modes that span three layers: knowledge graph construction (bad extraction, missed entities), retrieval (wrong graph traversal, poor vector search), and generation (hallucination, context overflow).

veerarag.title: 11. Production: Failures, Scale & Security: Scalability & Performance

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Activation Functions
veeraml.summary: Activation functions are the non-linear transformations that give neural networks their power. Without them, even deep networks would collapse into simple linear models.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Forward & Backward Propagation
veeraml.summary: Backpropagation is the algorithm that makes deep learning possible. It efficiently computes gradients for all parameters in a neural network using the chain rule of calculus.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Deep Learning Loss Functions
veeraml.summary: Loss functions (or cost functions) measure how well your model's predictions match the true labels. They are the optimization objective that guides learning through backpropagation.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Weight Initialization
veeraml.summary: Weight initialization is one of the most critical yet often overlooked aspects of training neural networks.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Gradient Issues (Vanishing & Exploding Gradients)
veeraml.summary: Gradient problems are the main obstacles to training deep neural networks. They occur when gradients become extremely small (vanishing) or extremely large (exploding) as they propagate backward through layers, making training impossible.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Batch Normalization
veeraml.summary: Batch Normalization (BatchNorm) is one of the most impactful innovations in deep learning.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Dropout & Regularization in Deep Learning
veeraml.summary: Regularization prevents overfitting - when a model learns training data too well but fails to generalize to new data. In deep learning with millions of parameters, overfitting is a constant threat.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Gradient Descent Variants
veeraml.summary: Gradient Descent is the fundamental optimization algorithm for training neural networks. However, the basic version has limitations.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Advanced Optimizers
veeraml.summary: Beyond basic gradient descent, advanced optimizers use momentum, adaptive learning rates, and other techniques to dramatically improve training speed and stability. These algorithms are the workhorses of modern deep learning.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Learning Rate Strategies
veeraml.summary: The learning rate is the most important hyperparameter in deep learning. Too large → training diverges.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Training Stability
veeraml.summary: Training instability can derail your deep learning project. Exploding gradients, NaN losses, and diverging training are common nightmares.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Mixed Precision Training
veeraml.summary: Mixed precision training uses both FP16 (half precision) and FP32 (single precision) to train models 2x faster with ~50% less memory, while maintaining accuracy. This is now standard practice in modern deep learning.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Gradient Accumulation
veeraml.summary: Gradient accumulation allows training with large effective batch sizes without requiring massive GPU memory. It's essential for training large models and achieving stable optimization when hardware is limited.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Training Checkpointing
veeraml.summary: Training checkpointing is essential for saving and resuming long training runs. It prevents data loss from crashes, enables experimentation, and allows continued training across sessions.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Hyperparameter Tuning for Deep Learning
veeraml.summary: Hyperparameter tuning is the process of finding the best configuration for your model. Unlike model parameters (learned during training), hyperparameters are set before training begins.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Convolution Operations
veeraml.summary: Convolution is the fundamental operation in CNNs that enables spatial feature detection. Unlike fully connected layers, convolutions preserve spatial relationships and are translation-invariant.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Pooling Layers
veeraml.summary: Pooling layers downsample feature maps, reducing spatial dimensions while retaining important features. They provide translation invariance and reduce computation.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Classic CNN Architectures
veeraml.summary: Learn the foundational CNN architectures that shaped computer vision: LeNet-5, AlexNet, and VGG. These architectures established the core principles used in modern deep learning.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: ResNet and Skip Connections
veeraml.summary: ResNet (Residual Networks) solved the degradation problem of very deep networks through skip connections. This breakthrough enabled training networks with 100+ layers.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: Modern CNNs, Visualization, Transfer Learning & Augmentation
veeraml.summary: ACTIVATION MAPS Visualize feature maps after convolution.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: RNN Fundamentals
veeraml.summary: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) process sequential data by maintaining hidden state across time steps. Unlike feedforward networks, RNNs have loops that allow information to persist.

veeraml.title: 09. Deep Learning: LSTM, GRU, Bidirectional RNNs, Seq2Seq & Applications
veeraml.summary: Problem with vanilla RNNs: Vanishing gradients → Can't learn long-term dependencies; Memory limited to ~10 timesteps
